In [[algebraic geometry]], a '''crepant resolution'''  of a [[mathematical singularity|singularity]] is a [[resolution of singularities|resolution]] that does not affect the [[canonical class]] of the [[manifold]]. The term "crepant" was coined by {{harvs |txt |last=Reid |first=Miles |authorlink=Miles Reid |year=1983}} by removing the prefix "dis" from the word "discrepant", to indicate that the resolutions have no [[Discrepancy (algebraic geometry)|discrepancy]] in the canonical class.

The '''crepant resolution conjecture''' of {{harvtxt|Ruan|2006}} states that the orbifold cohomology of a [[Daniel Gorenstein|Gorenstein]] [[orbifold]] is isomorphic to a semiclassical limit of the quantum cohomology of a crepant resolution.

In 2 dimensions, crepant resolutions of complex Gorenstein quotient singularities ([[du Val singularities]]) always exist and are unique, in 3 dimensions they exist<ref>T. Bridgeland, A. King, M. Reid. ''J. Amer. Math. Soc.'' 14 (2001), 535-554. Theorem 1.2.</ref> but need not be unique as they can be related by [[flop (algebraic geometry)|flop]]s, and in dimensions greater than 3 they need not exist.

A substitute for crepant resolutions which always exists is a '''terminal model'''. Namely, for every variety ''X'' over a field of characteristic zero such that ''X'' has [[Canonical singularity|canonical]] singularities (for example, [[Rational singularity|rational]] Gorenstein singularities), there is a variety ''Y'' with '''Q'''-factorial [[Canonical singularity|terminal]] singularities and a [[Birational geometry|birational]] projective morphism ''f'': ''Y'' → ''X'' which is crepant in the sense that ''K''<sub>''Y''</sub> = ''f''*''K''<sub>''X''</sub>.<ref>C. Birkar, P. Cascini, C. Hacon, J. McKernan. ''J. Amer. Math. Soc.'' 23 (2010), 405-468. Corollary 1.4.3.</ref>
